output.brief:
The brake complaints most likely come from contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, the Tessaro pads or the hills. Northfield Motor Services serviced 13 Eastgate vans while your in-house brake bay was closed. Eleven of them got fluid from an old bulk drum with a missing cap, and that fluid had absorbed water. Those 11 vans are exactly the 11 vans behind all 27 complaints. The two Northfield vans that got fluid from a new drum had no complaints. Two warranty-returned vans tested at about 150°C boiling point, against 255°C for sealed stock. Northfield emailed Larkspur on 25 September recommending a recheck of the other vans, and nobody replied. The same drivers had no brake problems in other vans, including on Upper Wend. Calder Road vans also use Tessaro pads and had no complaints.

I'm fairly sure (about 90%). What to do this week:
- Pull the Northfield-serviced vans from service. Test their fluid and renew it from sealed stock.
- Don't discipline drivers. Their reports were accurate, and discipline would discourage reporting.
- Check the fluid on the Calder Road vans at their next service.
- Hold off on switching pad supplier until squeal data on fresh pads of both brands exists.
